notice: RN bank batch 123: Hematologic and oncologic case studies: pernicious anemia, spinal cord compression, extravasation and TTP, with four standalone items. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md.

questions.stem: After reading the note, complete the diagram with the condition the client is most likely experiencing, the 2 actions the nurse should take first, and the 2 parameters to monitor.

actions.text: Give calcium gluconate IV as prescribed
Give regular insulin with dextrose IV as prescribed
Give sodium polystyrene as the only treatment
Encourage the client to drink orange juice
Start lactated Ringer's at a fast rate

rationale.correct: Peaked T waves and a wide QRS with potassium 7.2 need calcium and an insulin shift now.

perOption.c1: Potassium 7.2 with peaked T waves and a wide QRS.
perOption.c2: Would not explain the ECG pattern this strongly.
perOption.a1: Stabilizes the heart membrane in minutes.
perOption.a3: Too slow alone for these ECG changes.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: A client receiving chemotherapy has blood counts each week. For each trend, choose the interpretation.

options.text: Nadir around day 10; neutropenic precautions now
A slow fall; monitor for fatigue

rationale.correct: Neutrophils and platelets reach their nadir around days 7 to 14; precautions match the counts.

perOption.b1:a: The lowest point is when infection risk peaks.
perOption.b2:c: Usually only below 10,000 or with bleeding.
perOption.b3:a: Red cells live longer, so they fall slowly.

questions.stem: On an oncology unit at the start of the shift, four clients have needs. Whose bedside should the nurse go to first?

options.text: A client with leukemia whose platelet count is 18,000/mm3 and who has a few petechiae on the shins
A client with lung cancer who reports new back pain and leg heaviness since the night
A client with lymphoma whose antiemetic is due before the 0900 chemotherapy
A client with colon cancer who asks to talk about stopping treatment and going home

rationale.correct: New back pain with leg symptoms in a client with cancer is cord compression until proven otherwise.

perOption.a: Expected with this count; maintain bleeding precautions.
perOption.b: Possible spinal cord compression; delay causes permanent paralysis.
perOption.d: Important; arrange time after the urgent client.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

options.text: Weighing clients on the same scale before breakfast

questions.stem: On day 3 of B12 injections, the client reports muscle weakness and palpitations. Review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Place the client on a cardiac monitor as prescribed
Stop the B12 permanently because of the reaction
Give an extra B12 injection to speed up recovery of the nerves

rationale.correct: Red cell production uses potassium; replace it and monitor.

perOption.a: Hypokalemia from rapid red cell production.
perOption.d: This is an expected effect of recovery, not an allergy.

caseStudies.title: Pernicious anemia compared with iron deficiency

exhibits.title: Primary care
exhibits.body: A 68-year-old client reports 4 months of tiredness, a sore tongue, and numbness and tingling in both feet. The client has stumbled twice in the dark and has been more forgetful. The client takes metformin and omeprazole and has autoimmune hypothyroidism.

exhibits.title: Phone call and arrival
exhibits.body: A 63-year-old client with prostate cancer that has spread to the bones calls about 2 weeks of worsening mid-back pain that is worse lying down and at night. Today both legs feel heavy and the client has not passed urine since the morning.

rows.label: Back pain
cells: 8/10 at the T8 level, worse lying flat and with coughing

caseStudies.title: Vesicant chemotherapy extravasation and hazardous-drug safety

exhibits.title: Chemotherapy chair
exhibits.body: A 47-year-old client with breast cancer is receiving doxorubicin by IV push through a peripheral IV in the left forearm because the port is blocked. Halfway through, the client says the site burns.

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 32-year-old client comes in with tiredness, bruises on the legs and a headache. The partner says the client has been confused since the morning and had a brief episode of slurred speech.
